text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Politburo member Pham The Duyet, on a Christmas-time visit to a Catholic commune in Ha Tay province, stressed the leading role of the Communist Party and mass organisations in strengthening solidarity between Catholics and non-Catholics to boost local economic and cultural development.
-- State-run Petrvietnam has pumped ashore about 8.6 million tonnes of crude oil so far this year, 300,000 more than targeted.

-- Only two-thirds of the planned 1996/97 winter-spring rice crop has been planted in the Mekong Delta due to irregular weather patterns, most notably late annual flooding. The region produces half of the nation's food and is a major supplier of agricultural products for export.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai and Egyptian Vice Minister of Agriculture Fikry El-Kirby held talks to boost cooperation in rice, sugar cane and cotton production.
-- Some 5,900 people were killed and 21,700 injured in 20,000 traffic accidents in Vietnam in 1996.
-- The police force has established plans to maintain social order and security during the Tet lunar new year festive period.
-- More than 60 hotels, restaurants and massage parlours and four karaoke bars in Hanoi were closed as part of this year's anti-socil evils campaign.
